findings.title: Stored XSS in admin-mini.html — referral form fields injected into admin DOM unescaped (token theft chain)
findings.description: admin-mini.html has NO HTML-escaping helper anywhere. In the referral panel, fields submitted via the PUBLIC unauthenticated endpoint /api/referral/register (full_name, location, phone, interests, reject_reason) are interpolated directly into innerHTML. Any anonymous attacker can register a referral with full_name='' and the payload executes in the admin's session when the admin opens the referral tab. Because the admin session bearer token is stored in localStorage (see FE-002), the script can exfiltrate the admin token and fully take over the panel. This is a stored XSS -> admin account takeover chain.
findings.fix: Add an escHtml() helper (same as student.html lines 2753-2761) and wrap EVERY server/user value in innerHTML templates: ${escHtml(r.full_name)}, r.location, r.phone, r.interests, r.reject_reason, r.group_name, r.mars_id, etc. Apply across the whole file.

findings.title: admin-mini.html stores admin session bearer token in localStorage (stealable via XSS)
findings.description: The mini-admin session token (_sessionToken) is persisted in localStorage ('miniAdminToken') and read back on load (line 340). localStorage is fully readable by any injected script. Combined with the unescaped innerHTML sinks (FE-001, FE-003), an XSS payload trivially steals the admin token and replays it against /api/admin/* endpoints. localStorage tokens also survive long-term, widening the window for theft.
findings.fix: Prefer not to persist a long-lived admin token in localStorage. Since the app already authenticates via Telegram X-Init-Data, rely on initData and use a short-lived in-memory token, or an HttpOnly cookie issued by the server. At minimum, eliminate all XSS sinks (FE-001/FE-003) so the token cannot be read by injected scripts.

findings.title: Stored XSS in admin-mini.html — student/leaderboard/audit data injected into admin DOM unescaped
findings.description: Throughout admin-mini.html, server data is placed into innerHTML with no escaping: student list (s.full_name, s.group_name, s.mars_id at lines 756-757), student detail sheet (s.full_name, s.username, s.phone at 775,781-783), leaderboard names (s.full_name, s.group_name at 1152-1153) and audit logs (x.action, x.target, x.details at 1722-1723). full_name/username originate from students who control those values (registration, Telegram username), so a malicious student name executes script in the admin context. Same token-theft impact as FE-001.
findings.fix: Wrap all of these in escHtml(). Use .textContent where a node holds a single value. Audit log action/target/details must also be escaped.

findings.title: XSS in games.html game leaderboard — other users' full_name/group_name injected unescaped
findings.description: loadGameLeaderboard() injects l.full_name and l.group_name (other students' names) directly into innerHTML with no escaping. games.html has no escHtml helper. A student with a crafted display name executes script in every other student's WebApp session. student.html's equivalent leaderboard correctly uses escHtml (lines 3861-3862), so this is an inconsistency/regression.
findings.fix: Add an escHtml() helper to games.html and wrap ${l.full_name} and ${l.group_name}.

findings.title: Broken onclick handlers / attribute injection — group & student names with apostrophes inside single-quoted inline handlers
findings.description: Group names and other server strings are embedded inside single-quoted inline handlers, e.g. onclick="_studentFilter='${g}';..." (748), confirmApproveRef(${id},'${g}') (1265), and the student filter chips. Uzbek names/groups very commonly contain an apostrophe (O'quvchi, G'ayrat). An apostrophe terminates the JS string and breaks the handler (functional bug) and is an attribute-injection vector. curator.html's esc() (line 1719) also does NOT escape the single quote, so its many onclick="openSheet('${esc(s.mars_id)}')" handlers have the same exposure for any value containing '.
findings.fix: Avoid building inline handlers from dynamic strings: attach listeners via addEventListener and pass values via data-* attributes, or pass an index/id and look up the object. If keeping inline handlers, ensure the escape function also encodes ' as ' AND JS-escapes for the attribute context.

findings.title: curator.html — href and avatar built from student data without escaping
findings.description: Attendance list builds a Telegram link as href="${tgUrl}" where tgUrl is derived from raw s.username (line 1869-1872) with no escaping; a username containing a quote/space breaks out of the attribute. Also avatars use s.full_name.charAt(0).toUpperCase() unescaped (lines 1610, 1628 via textContent is fine but 1610/1884/1932 are innerHTML) — single char so low impact, but inconsistent with the esc() used elsewhere on the same line.
findings.fix: Escape username for the href attribute (encodeURIComponent for the path segment and esc for attribute context), and run esc() on the first-letter avatar in innerHTML contexts.

findings.title: Double-submit / race not guarded on chat send and game score save
findings.description: sendChatMessage() (student.html 5177) clears the input then awaits the POST but does not disable the send button, so rapid taps can fire multiple POSTs (duplicate messages). games.html saveScore() (802) and recordPlay() are also called without a submit guard, allowing duplicate score submissions on fast double-tap of the game-over button. curator.html sendMessage() and admin doLogin DO correctly disable the button (good pattern to mirror).
findings.fix: Disable the send/submit button (or use an in-flight boolean flag) at the start of the async handler and re-enable in finally, matching the pattern in curator.html sendMessage (lines 1991-2016).
findings.snippet: async function sendChatMessage() { const inp=...; inp.value=''; await api('/chat',{...}); }  // no button disable

findings.title: student.html homework view interpolates hw.group_name without escaping
findings.description: loadHomework() escapes most fields elsewhere but injects ${hw.group_name} raw into innerHTML at line 3575 while the rest of the file consistently uses escHtml. group_name is server-controlled/admin-set, lower risk than student-controlled fields, but it is an inconsistency that should be closed.

findings.title: Some fetch() calls lack error handling, can leave UI stuck on spinner
findings.description: recordPlay() (student.html 2848) calls fetch + res.json() with no try/catch; a network failure rejects the promise. Callers mostly use .catch(()=>{}) so it is contained, but loadReferral() (2908) only console.errors and leaves spinners/empty placeholders without a user-visible error state. games.html loadGameLeaderboard catch is empty (742) leaving a stale spinner if the first load fails. Most other paths handle errors well (api() wrappers throw and callers render an error empty-state).
findings.fix: Wrap raw fetch helpers in try/catch and render an explicit error/retry state instead of leaving spinners; give loadReferral a visible error message.
findings.snippet: async function recordPlay(gameType){ const r = await fetch('/api/game/record-play', {...}); const data = await r.json(); ... }

summary: student.html and curator.html are reasonably well built (escHtml/esc helpers, api() wrappers with error handling, chat poll interval cleaned up, login/send buttons disabled, tg.ready/expand called). The serious problems are in admin-mini.html: it has NO HTML-escaping helper and injects student-, leaderboard-, audit- and PUBLIC referral-form data straight into innerHTML, while persisting the admin session bearer token in localStorage — a stored-XSS-to-admin-takeover chain that any anonymous user can trigger via /api/referral/register (FE-001/002/003, critical). games.html repeats the unescaped-leaderboard XSS (FE-004). Secondary issues: dynamic strings inside single-quoted inline onclick handlers break on Uzbek apostrophes and allow attribute injection (FE-005), unescaped href/avatar in curator (FE-006), missing double-submit guards on chat send / game score (FE-007), one unescaped field in student homework (FE-008), and a few fetch paths without error states (FE-009). Priority: add an escHtml helper to admin-mini.html and games.html, escape every interpolated server value, and stop trusting localStorage for the admin token.
